A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same character-level robustness study, with substantial revision in v3. All 23 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable. Retained methods, numerical tables, and figures support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations on Luogu coding problems, GSM8K, and Chinese GSM8K, together with perturbation ablations and internal-model analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original UCC-Inj results and reports additional typo, shuffling, randomized-tokenization, and rewriting-control experiments on GSM8K.

M1.justification: The UCC-Inj procedure is retained, but v3 Section 2 adds two substantial perturbation procedures: sequential deletion, substitution, swapping, and insertion within selected words, and random within-word character shuffling. This expands the investigated method family without changing the underlying LLM architectures or training.

E1.justification: v3 adds typo-corrupted and character-shuffled mathematical-input scenarios, while removing the 100-problem Luogu coding evaluation and GSM8K_zh comparison. Reported task coverage consequently concentrates on GSM8K mathematics. OCR and low-resource languages are discussed as applications, not evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: v3 directly compares Typo-Method, Shuffle-Method, and UCC-Inj on GSM8K, including the prefix experiment in Table 2. The asterisk and 8-/27-symbol ASCII insertion alternatives evaluated in v1 Figure 6 disappear, while the comparison between inserted A characters and variation selectors remains.

E3.justification: New protocols vary corruption over 30/50/70/100% of eligible words, independently tokenize randomly split word fragments, and introduce Must-Rewrite versus No-Rewrite instructions. The dedicated model-size sweep and prefix table now use non-thinking mode; Qwen3-0.6B gains perturbation evaluations, while Qwen2.5 and 8B Llama attack curves disappear. Shared decoding and answer-scoring settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds individual typo-operation ablations, randomized-segmentation diagnostics, rewriting controls, and typo/shuffle response categorization (Figure 4; Tables 4, 6, 11). It drops randomized-insertion-count, Chinese-language, and several visible-noise analyses. The layer-wise feature-similarity analysis disappears; the prefix-similarity trend remains described, but its supporting plot is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added response-category percentages extend the existing descriptive reporting practice rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include DeepSeek-Reasoner accuracy of 0.904 under 100-Shuffle and 0.160 under 100-Typo, plus randomized-segmentation accuracies of 0.935 for Qwen3-30B and 0.932 for Llama3.1-70B. Luogu and randomized-insertion results disappear. The six shared UCC-Inj table rows and full character-tokenization table remain numerically identical. Clean prefix2 accuracy changes from 0.935 to 0.035 in v1 Table 1 versus v3 Table 2, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs, and no substantive mathematical derivation or assumption changes. The new RoPE and reconstruction explanations are qualitative mechanism interpretations.

C1.justification: v1 centers UCC-Inj, its anti-cheating motivation, and robustness to inserted noise. v3 reframes the contribution around three perturbation classes, extends robustness claims to randomized subword segmentation, and foregrounds perturbation-specific mechanisms. Anti-cheating becomes one secondary application in Appendix A.

C2.justification: v3 adds perceptibility-based explanations of rewriting, a RoPE-continuity explanation for shuffle robustness, and an information-loss explanation for typo failures. It qualifies rewriting benefits under stronger corruption and expands prospective OCR and low-resource-language applications. The single-perturbation limitation is removed, while architectural and training-related uncertainties receive more explicit discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds a concrete substitution lookup table and specifications for the new perturbation and segmentation procedures. It removes v1's code-access link and reproducibility statement, Luogu prompt, and ASCII-noise lists. Shared model URLs, API-use information, prompting details, and decoding parameters are retained; repository availability itself cannot be inferred from the omitted link.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from anti-cheating and detection toward character-level adversarial robustness and internal diagnosis. v3 adds TextBugger, PromptRobust, Rocamora et al.'s character-attack study, RoFormer, and other perturbation research, while removing detector literature and the Elhage/Olsson mechanism references. The introduction now emphasizes a claimed gap in fine-grained behavioral and internal analyses.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial mechanism passages are extensively rewritten. The standalone motivating-application section disappears, mechanism subsections are reorganized, and the appendices are restructured around a new broader-impact section. The title and author line also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text, replaces Figure 1, rebuilds Figures 2–3 around three perturbation methods, and adds summary, diagnostic, and substitution tables. The retained A-insertion panels become separate Figures 6–7. Existing tokenization results, response-category charts, and the attention heatmap are relocated or resized, while language and feature-similarity plots disappear.

improvement.justification: The typo/shuffle experiments and segmentation/rewriting controls address v1's acknowledged narrow perturbation coverage. However, v3 loses coding and Chinese-language evaluations and feature-similarity plots while advancing additional mechanism explanations without corresponding causal tests. Reporting also becomes less reliable: Table 2 changes clean prefix2 accuracy from 0.935 to 0.035 despite claiming prefix robustness, and Section 3 assigns 57.5% to 3-Inj although Table 7 places it under 1-Inj. These substantial benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
